# Changelog — Cookbook

## 0.6.1

- Notifications: on large screens the list now opens right under the bell; on phones and tablets it stays centred on the screen. It always fits the screen: the heading stays in view and only the list scrolls.

## 0.6.0

- Share a recipe with everyone: a **public link** on the recipe’s page opens it for anyone, also without a DevQuake account, with buttons for WhatsApp, Facebook, Pinterest, X and more. It shows the recipe, its photo and your name; you can stop it at any time.

## 0.5.1

- When a member removes their DevQuake account, what they added to your things (comments, items, ticks, photos…) stays, shown as “REMOVED_…” instead of their name.

## 0.5.0

- Pictures load faster: lists and previews show small versions, and tapping a picture opens it in full size.
- “Back” links now return to the page you came from, with its filters and where you had scrolled to.

## 0.4.0

- Add your own picture of an ingredient while writing a recipe (“Your picture”, camera or library). Only you see it, next to that ingredient in every recipe.
- The DevQuake team can choose a member’s picture to show everyone instead of the drawn one; the drawn pictures always stay.

## 0.3.0

- Ingredients now have small drawn pictures: next to each ingredient of a recipe and in the suggestions when you link an ingredient.
- Many more ingredients to link to, with nutrition and allergens: fresh and dried herbs, spices and seeds, vegetables, fruit, nuts, pulses, grains, dairy, meat, fish and kitchen basics — over 190 in all.

## 0.2.0

- The app’s card on DevQuake and its front page now show how many members use it and its totals: recipes, recommendations.

0.1.0

- A starter library of recipes written for DevQuake, in English, German, Romanian and Hungarian, from shakshuka to goulash soup.
- Choose the servings and every quantity is recalculated: eggs stay whole, spices grow less, quantities are rounded for the kitchen. Metric or imperial.
- Nutrition per portion, diets with the reason they fit (for example “28 g protein per portion”) and the 14 EU allergens.
- Cooking mode: one step per screen in big text, timers that beep, a voice that reads the steps, and the screen stays on.
- Write your own recipes with a photo, link ingredients to the nutrition table, keep them private or share them with a link. Save a copy of any recipe to change it, and keep favourites.
- Works with your shopping lists: tick what you have and put the rest on a list in one step.
- Make your recipes public: everyone using the Cookbook can recommend them and leave a comment, which reaches you as a notification and in your messages on DevQuake. Every 100 recommendations of your recipe earn you an NPS point.
- Recipes are easier to follow: a “Get ready” list (equipment and how to prepare each ingredient), steps grouped into prepare, cook and serve with the ingredients each needs, also in cooking mode.
- A guided editor in four steps with suggestions and a checklist of what others need to cook your recipe.
- Plan a recipe straight into a meal of your Meal planner week.
